bible.title: Crescent Cove
bible.intent: A small, sunny, natural tropical island built from this world's own brief and mood board. One coherent first area you walk rather than look at: a pale crescent beach around clear turquoise shallows, a shaded stop at a thatched shelter and timber jetty at the west end, and a path up the limestone headland at the east end to a rewarding summit view over the lagoon, reef and distant islands. Aim for higher fidelity than earlier examples while staying honest about what the runtime can show.
bible.rules:
FIRST AREA AND ROUTE
1. One walkable first area only: arrival on the beach -> west along the crescent to the shelter and jetty -> back east along the beach -> up a looping headland path to a summit viewpoint -> return the same way. The route must be continuous, readable and walkable by the maker actor (slopes under 45 degrees with margin; aim for 20 degrees or less on paths, steps 0.35 m or less).
2. The shelter is the shaded stop: thatched roof on timber posts, table and bench in shade, facing the lagoon and jetty. The jetty is low and weathered on round posts, short, stepping from dry sand into knee-deep water (about 0.4-0.6 m at the end at rest).
3. The summit is the reward: a clear, unobstructed view across the whole bay, reef edge and distant islands; protect that sightline from palms and rocks.
4. Palm grove sits behind the beach as a backdrop and shade band; keep paths, the shelter approach and the summit sightline clear of trunks.

WATER
5. Depth must read from both the beach and the summit: shallow turquoise over pale sand near shore, grading through cyan to deep blue past the reef edge. Depth comes from real terrain depth under the water, not painted colour alone.
6. Movement is gentle: small, long, slow waves in the lagoon; no stormy chop. A soft foam line where water meets sand.
7. Coral heads read as scattered dark patches in the lagoon from above and as textured forms when wading; keep a sand corridor clear for wading from the jetty.
8. Fish swim near shore in small, calm schools in the shallows, visible from the beach and jetty. Fish are a target; they only count once actually observed moving in the runtime.

SKY AND LIGHT
9. Bright, high tropical sun, warm but natural; soft white cumulus clouds overhead are the target. Haze only for the far horizon, never fogging the bay.

PALETTE AND MATERIALS (from the material card)
10. Sand: coarse pale cream with a few grey and shell grains; darker, cooler wet band at the waterline.
11. Limestone: porous, pitted coral limestone, cream with grey, ochre staining low on rocks; never smooth or uniform grey.
12. Timber: silver-brown, cracked, weathered driftwood planks with visible gaps and bolts; no fresh or varnished wood.
13. Palm: glossy green fronds with a yellow midrib on slim, curving, leaning trunks; thatch in dry straw tones.

SCALE
14. Human scale throughout: eye height 1.72 m, paths 1.2-2 m wide, shelter roof eaves about 2.2-2.5 m, table about 0.75 m, jetty deck about 0.5-0.7 m above the water surface at rest.

SCENERY AND LIMITS
15. Distant islands and offshore rocks are non-walkable scenery: placed far out, low detail, no route to them. The outer reef and deep water are the edge of the explorable area.
16. The cove stays an origin-layer workspace that can be hidden; terrain and water must work with it hidden.

HONESTY
17. The references are AI-generated inspiration, not engine renders, photographs of a real place, or measured plans. Proportions in them are suggestive.
18. Make no claim that any build matches the references photographically.
19. Keep targets (these rules), implemented behaviour, measured results (world_sample, world_check, world_observe, renderer metrics) and owner acceptance as separate findings. A proposal is not applied until world_observe shows its revision.
20. Missing runtime capabilities are logged as gaps, never faked with props that imply behaviour that does not exist.

BUILD SPLIT (priority order)
Holodeck terrain/water/environment: (a) heightfield island: beach crescent, lagoon basin with sand shelf, reef rim, drop-off to deep water, headland mass and path grades; (b) ocean water with gentle waves, shallow/deep colours and foam; (c) sun position, sky and light; (d) maker possession for walking, wading and the summit route.
Kiln assets: (1) coconut palm with named frond meshes for foliage wind; (2) limestone headland rocks: large karst cluster, medium boulder group, small half-buried rocks; (3) thatched shelter with table and bench; (4) jetty modules: deck on round posts, wide platform, three-step stair; (5) headland path pieces (rock steps/edging) where terrain grade alone is not enough; (6) coral heads (staghorn on live rock, finger coral) and seagrass clump; (7) reef fish (damselfish, butterflyfish, jack) if a usable swimming behaviour exists; (8) beach scatter: driftwood, shells, low coastal shrubs; (9) distant islands and offshore rocks as low-detail scenery.
